layers.name: Deep Water Base
layers.description: The foundational deep blue-grey of the river water.
layers.paintingTip: Apply a broad wash of Indigo and Payne's Gray using a 2-inch flat brush. Keep the paper slightly damp to allow for soft edges in later layers.

layers.name: Sunset Sky Reflections
layers.description: Warm golden and orange tones reflected from the sky onto the water surface.
layers.paintingTip: Using a wet-on-wet technique, drop in Raw Sienna and Quinacridone Gold. Focus on the vertical shimmering column in the upper third.

layers.name: Blue Sky Tones
layers.description: Lighter blue reflections that break up the dark water and warm tones.
layers.paintingTip: Use a round brush with Cerulean Blue. Use horizontal, slightly wavy strokes to mimic the surface tension of the water.

layers.name: Wake and Ripples
layers.description: Darker shadows created by the movement of the kayak and the paddle strokes.
layers.paintingTip: Switch to a smaller rigger brush with a concentrated mix of Neutral Tint. Paint the concentric circles and the V-shape trailing the boat.

layers.name: The Red Kayak
layers.description: The main focal point: a bright red sea kayak.
layers.paintingTip: Use Cadmium Red Medium. Paint the sharp, elongated diamond shape. Leave a small sliver of white paper for the highlight on the left edge.

layers.name: The Paddler
layers.description: The figure in the kayak, including the torso and the white sun hat.
layers.paintingTip: Use Titanium White for the hat and a mix of Alizarin Crimson for the life vest. Keep the shapes simple and gestural.

layers.name: The Paddle
layers.description: The black double-bladed paddle stretched across the kayak.
layers.paintingTip: Use a thin liner brush with Ivory Black. Ensure the line is straight but the blades have a slight curve.

layers.name: Surface Glints
layers.description: Sharp white and light blue highlights where the sun catches the tips of small ripples.
layers.paintingTip: Use dry brush technique with thick Chinese White or white gouache. Drag the brush quickly across the paper to catch only the texture peaks.
